newsitem.title: USA: Albright sees new initiative for ex-Soviet states.
newsitem.headline: Albright sees new initiative for ex-Soviet states.

text.p: The Clinton administration plans an initiative designed to move ex-Soviet states, especially Russia, from economic stability to economic growth, Secretary of State-designate Madeleine Albright says.

Answering more than 200 written questions posed by the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, she said that one of the critical U.S. national security interests during the next four years is the future of the newly independent states (NIS) of the former Soviet Union.

As a result, "we will seek funding for a new Partnership for Freedom initiative, the centerpiece of which is a package of measures built to move the NIS, particularly Russia, from economic stability to economic growth," she said.

Albright said this initiative, to be outlined in President Clinton's 1998 budget due out soon, would concentrate heavily on trade, investment and anti-crime programs, as well as environment and energy." She gave no more details.

The Senate Foreign Relations Committee on Monday voted to recommend that Albright's nomination to be the first woman secretary of state be approved by the full Senate, which is expected to act on Wednesday.
